summary: A public e-petition by Mohamed Saud asks Parliament to end the special health insurance that current and former MPs, their spouses and children under 18 receive at public expense. Under Law No. 5/2013 on Parliament's privileges and powers, this cover lasts for life and pays for treatment in the Maldives, SAARC and ASEAN countries. The petition compares this with the US, Japan, Germany and Australia, where it says MPs use the same health system as the public or lose special cover soon after leaving office. It asks that all MPs instead use the national Aasandha scheme like other citizens.
keyPoints: Coverage under the law extends to 19 countries, including Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore, per the petition.
Former MPs keep the insurance for life under the retirement benefits chapter of Law No. 5/2013.
Germany is cited as giving former MPs a health insurance subsidy for only 18 months after leaving office.
Requested change: amend the laws so no MP or MP's family gets health benefits paid from taxes that ordinary Maldivians do not get.
Petition reference EPT202600052; referred by the Petition Committee for floor debate.
outcome: Referred by the Petition Committee for debate on the floor; still ongoing
